title: X++ declarations: const vs readonly, var inference, loop scope, the shadowing rejection, prmIsDefault
instruction: In the sandbox model, create a class DemoRetryPolicy that shows how X++ declarations and scope actually work. Ground it first with get_knowledge(topic="xpp-declarations"). Shape: (1) a `public const int MaxAttempts = 5;` field - a compile-time constant with its initializer at the declaration, which is what replaces a macro here; a `#define` FAILS this case. (2) a `readonly int timeoutSec;` field assigned in `new()` and never again - the doc comment must say why readonly and not const (the value is only known per instance). (3) a `protected void new(int _timeoutSec)` plus a `public static DemoRetryPolicy construct(int _timeoutSec)` factory. (4) `public int totalBudget()` - a `for (int i = 0; i < MaxAttempts; i++)` loop whose counter is declared in the for-init, so it is scoped to the loop; summing timeoutSec into a local. Then a second loop NESTED inside that one, which needs its own counter: nesting is what makes the rule bite, because the X++ compiler rejects shadowing an outer variable outright, so the inner counter must be renamed rather than hidden - say so in a comment. (A sibling loop after the first may legally reuse the name; only a nested block may not.) (5) `public str describe(str _prefix = '')` - an optional parameter. It must distinguish "caller passed an empty string" from "caller passed nothing" with prmIsDefault, and build its result with strFmt from a label. (6) `public container snapshot()` - uses `var` for one local whose type is obvious from its initializer, and a plainly typed declaration for one where it is not; `var` without an initializer is a compile error and FAILS this case. Confirm every member signature you are unsure of with get_object_info before writing it. The class must build with zero errors and zero BP errors.
